coverage.subtopic: Vertical membrane-cytoskeleton linkage failure and increased osmotic fragility
coverage.learning_objective: Defects in vertical erythrocyte membrane-cytoskeleton interactions cause membrane loss, spherocyte formation, splenic sequestration, and increased osmotic fragility.

coverage.subtopic: NADPH-dependent glutathione regeneration during oxidant stress
coverage.learning_objective: G6PD-derived NADPH maintains reduced glutathione in erythrocytes; deficiency permits oxidant injury, Heinz body formation, and bite-cell hemolysis.

coverage.subtopic: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency and persistence of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers
coverage.learning_objective: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency allows ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers to persist, causing platelet-rich microthrombi, thrombocytopenia, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.

coverage.subtopic: Platelet GPIb-mediated adhesion and stabilization of factor VIII
coverage.learning_objective: Von Willebrand factor supports platelet adhesion through GPIb and stabilizes factor VIII; deficiency therefore impairs primary hemostasis and can reduce factor VIII activity.

coverage.subtopic: CD40 ligand-dependent class switching and germinal-center formation
coverage.learning_objective: CD40 ligand on activated helper T cells is required for B-cell class switching, germinal-center formation, affinity maturation, and effective macrophage activation.

coverage.subtopic: NADPH oxidase failure and absent dihydrorhodamine fluorescence shift
coverage.learning_objective: Chronic granulomatous disease results from NADPH oxidase failure, causing absent superoxide generation and an abnormal dihydrorhodamine oxidative-burst assay.

coverage.subtopic: C5b-C9 membrane attack complex formation and recurrent Neisseria infection
coverage.learning_objective: Terminal complement components C5b through C9 form the membrane attack complex; deficiency prevents bacterial membrane pore formation and predisposes to recurrent invasive Neisseria infection.

coverage.subtopic: Circulating antigen-antibody complex deposition with classical complement consumption
coverage.learning_objective: Serum sickness is a type III hypersensitivity reaction in which circulating antigen-antibody complexes deposit in tissues, activate complement, recruit neutrophils, and consume C3 and C4.
